recommendations.thesis: REVISED DOWN TWICE. Research first overstated the case with the gasoline-only crack (-49.1%); the correct 3-2-1 measure is -25.3%. The red team then recomputed that measure from FRED (DGASNYH/DHOILNYH/DCOILWTICO, 2x gasoline + 1x heating oil, less WTI, monthly means) and found the published seasonality claim wrong in the thesis's favour. VERIFIED: refining margin fell from $48.64/bbl in October to $36.34 in November-to-date, -25.3%, because spot gasoline fell 16.4% while WTI fell 8.2%. CORRECTED: that is the 2nd-worst October-to-November change of the 16 since 2011, NOT 'the fastest in 15 years' — 2011 fell -40.9% ($32.52 to $19.22). The honest median change is -2.8% and the mean +0.1% (published as -2.0% and +3.1%). So the compression is abnormal — top 12% of the sample — but it is not unprecedented, and the one true precedent is instructive rather than disqualifying: after November 2011 the crack kept falling to $15.65 in December before reverting to $21-28 by February 2012, which is the path this trade needs over a 15-session horizon. The claim is mean reversion toward the $19.22 November median with $17/bbl of room, not an earnings cliff. VLO rallied 9.6% off its 11/06 close of 346.45 in the same week margin compressed, and sits below a 20-day (389.70) that has crossed under its 50-day (399.97).
recommendations.key_risk: The absolute margin is still roughly 1.9x normal — $36.34 is the 2nd-highest November of the 16 since 2011, behind only 2022's $49.22 — so VLO can post a strong quarter and this short can be right about the direction of margins and still lose. ADDED BY THE RED TEAM, the two risks the published idea did not name: (1) THIS IS A COUNTER-TREND SHORT. VLO has gone from $116.09 (2025-04-30) to a $461.52 high in nineteen months, close to 4x, and at 379.83 it still trades 28.9% ABOVE its own 200-day. Mean reversion is the thesis, but the trend being faded is powerful and the name has beaten estimates three quarters running (+12.3%, +22.7%, +32.2%). (2) THE TARGET'S LEVEL JUSTIFICATION DECAYS. The published idea anchors the 296.00 target to the 200-day at 294.76, but that average is rising $1.04 a session and reaches roughly 310 by the end of a 15-session horizon — it will be above the target, not below it. The target is retained at 296.00 anyway, and is NOT moved to rescue a ratio, because a static anchor exists underneath it: VLO closed between 280 and 320 for 24 sessions from 2026-07-08 to 2026-08-10. Read the target against that shelf, not against the moving average. Also: no dated catalyst inside the horizon (VLO does not report until late January), short equity requires a Robinhood margin account, and the 2.38 ATR stop sits 11.9% away on a 5.08%-ATR instrument.
recommendations.counter_argument: Two objections; the first is answered more weakly than published, the second is not answered at all. PARTLY ANSWERED — autumn crack compression is seasonal. Recomputed across 16 years of FRED data: the Oct-to-Nov 3-2-1 change has a median of -2.8% and a mean of +0.1%, and 2026's -25.3% ranks 2nd worst of 16. The published version of this claim (-2.0% median, +3.1% mean, 'worst prior year -15.1% in 2019', 'rank 1 of 15') was wrong: 2011 fell -40.9%. The move is still abnormal rather than calendar, which is what the thesis needs, but it is a top-12% event with a worse precedent on the record, not a record. That correction is why conviction is 2 rather than 3. NOT ANSWERED — the $36.34 level is the second-highest November in 16 years against a $19.22 median, so refiners remain very profitable and estimates may not need to fall at all. That is a genuine negative, it is why size is cut to 1.0%, and it is the reason this is a reversion trade rather than a distress trade.
